_: BATTLE BOTS: THE HEAD SHAPE TABLE (tier one, 2026-09-05).
WHY IT EXISTS. Mike, 5 September: 'Not a whole lot of variation going on with
the models. Was hoping people could make their own cute unique robots.' It was
measured, not felt: six of the eight shipped heads are one dome, all eight
boots are one boot, and the eight torsos share one outline exactly. Two
earlier runs proved the rule this file answers to: PROMPT CHANGES CANNOT BEAT
WHAT THE RULER DRAWS. So variation is bought by AUTHORING RULERS, and the
head is where it is bought first, because the head is 57 of every 100 pixels
of a robot at ring size.
WHAT A ROW IS. One SHAPE (the crown silhouette and the ears) and one MOUTH.
Eight shapes and five mouth kinds give eighteen head looks; two of them are
already live (round with a grille is the shipped design-1 head, box with a
grille is the shipped design-2 head) and carry draw:false, so the v3 bake
draws the other SIXTEEN.
WHAT THIS FILE MAY NOT CARRY. No eye override, no symmetry override, no judge
relaxation of any kind. Every head in this table keeps exactly two lamp eyes
on the design-one eye row at the design-one radius band, a blank forehead, the
crease lugs, the dome underside and its ink inside the full head width. That
is the whole reason scripts/sd/rank-part.py needs no rule moved for any of
them: a shape that would need a rule relaxed is refused from this table.
WHERE THE GEOMETRY LIVES. Here: the shape word, the mouth kind, the prompt
clause and the note. NOT here: a single coordinate. The drawing is
scripts/bots-bake-parts.mjs --out v3 (headPartsV3), because a ruler is a
drawing and a drawing that can be retuned from a config file is a drawing
nobody can reproduce.
_tier: Tier is RICHNESS and shape is IDENTITY, so the two axes are independent. This table is authored at tier one only; the richer tiers of each shape follow later and change appointments, never the silhouette.
_promptSeam: How a row reaches the model. scripts/sd/bots-sd-prompts.json owns the head's
subject, and two of its clauses are shape-dependent:
form      carries the crown words 'a rounded dome crown'
features  carries the mouth words below in mouthPhrase
The job emitter REPLACES those two exact substrings with this row's crown and
mouth clause and refuses if either substring is not found, so a matrix edit
that moves the wording breaks loudly instead of silently shipping the dome
mouthPhrase: a dark recessed slatted grille for a mouth, low on the face under the eyes

grille.prompt: a dark recessed slatted grille for a mouth, low on the face under the eyes
grille.notes: the shipped mouth: one dark bar of slats on the centre line, well under the eyes

widegrille.prompt: a wide dark recessed slatted grille for a mouth, spanning the face low under the eyes
widegrille.notes: the same bar carried out to the cheeks: the bucket's own mouth, and the only mouth that is wider than it is tall by more than two to one

smile.prompt: a dark recessed curved smile for a mouth, low on the face under the eyes
smile.notes: a crescent slot, tips curling up, the same dark hole material as the grille

o.prompt: a dark recessed round O mouth, low on the face under the eyes
o.notes: one round hole on the centre line; the smallest mouth in the table, so it is drawn large enough to survive ring size

zigzag.prompt: a dark recessed zigzag mouth, low on the face under the eyes
zigzag.notes: a saw-tooth slot; the cone's own mouth and the only mouth with a repeating rhythm

shapes.name: Round
shapes.prompt: a rounded dome crown with a round cup ear high on each side
shapes.notes: the shipped design-one head. Its crown is the baseline every other shape is a departure from, so it is in the table with its two new mouths and its own grille look is left alone.

looks.why: already live as head design 1; the bake does not redraw a shipped head

shapes.name: Box
shapes.prompt: a soft box crown with rounded corners and a round cup ear on each side
shapes.notes: the shipped design-two head. Squared above, domed below, as the whole-bot study demands.

looks.why: already live as head design 2; the bake does not redraw a shipped head

shapes.name: Bear
shapes.prompt: two big round cup ears that form the top of the head, a low rounded crown between them
shapes.notes: the ears ARE the crown: their tops are the apex of the whole figure and the head's own dome sits below them. The single biggest silhouette departure in the table and the one a player will name first.

shapes.name: TV
shapes.prompt: a soft box crown with a short aerial standing on top of it
shapes.notes: the aerial lives INSIDE the head room the canvas already carries: its tip is the apex, so the figure's height does not move and no other part has to be retuned.

shapes.name: Bell
shapes.prompt: a narrow rounded crown that flares out to the full width at the cheeks, like a bell
shapes.notes: the only shape whose width grows all the way down. The crease lugs still make the outer edge, so the thing that covers the shoulder cap is unchanged.

shapes.name: Bucket
shapes.prompt: a wide flat rim across the top like an upturned bucket, the head narrowing a little below it
shapes.notes: the rim is the top. It is the only shape that is widest at the crown, which is what makes it read at ring size against the dome.

shapes.name: Cone
shapes.prompt: a squat cone with a blunt rounded top, widening steadily down to the cheeks
shapes.notes: a straight-sided taper, so its silhouette is the one in the table with no curve on the sides at all.

shapes.name: Cat
shapes.prompt: two soft pointed ears at the top with short rounded tips, a rounded crown between them
shapes.notes: cuddly, not spiky: the tip of each ear is rounded off at about a bolt head across, and no point stands longer than that, so the head keeps reading as a clay toy and never as a weapon.

_bodies: THE BODY SHAPE TABLE: the TORSO and the ARM (lane T, 2026-09-05). The head
rows above live in `shapes` and keep the file's `slot: head` heading, which
is where this file started; the body rows live here, under `bodies`, so a
reader of either section can never be handed the other one by accident.
WHY IT EXISTS. The look-alike gate read the factory rulers and reported, of
the torso: eight files, ONE shape, all 28 pairs at 1.000. Not close, the
same outline eight times, because tier and design only ever changed what was
drawn ON the barrel and never the barrel. The arm came back as two shapes
across eight files with a typical pair at 0.830. PROMPT CHANGES CANNOT BEAT
WHAT THE RULER DRAWS, so the body buys its variation by AUTHORING RULERS.
WHAT A ROW IS. One SHAPE, one OUTLINE. There is no second axis here: the
head's mouth swap works because a mouth is a hole in a face, and a torso has
no equivalent. A panel line is not a shape, which is the whole finding this
table answers to.
WHAT THIS FILE MAY NOT CARRY. No judge relaxation of any kind. Every shape
keeps the contract's own proportion bands, the frozen pivots, the buried
skirt and, on the torso, the wind-up key at the importer's own anchor. That
is checked at bake time on the rendered pixels, not asserted here.
WHERE THE GEOMETRY LIVES. Here: the shape word, the prompt clause and the
note. NOT here: a single coordinate. The drawing is
scripts/bots-bake-parts.mjs --out v3 (torsoPartsV3 and armPartsV3), because
a ruler is a drawing and a drawing that can be retuned from a config file is
a drawing nobody can reproduce.

torso.formPhrase: a rounded barrel, half again wider than it is tall, shoulders rounded off, no neck

shapes.name: Barrel
shapes.prompt: a rounded barrel body, straight sides and big soft rounded corners, half again wider than it is tall, shoulders rounded off, no neck
shapes.notes: the shipped outline, and the only one of the four that is not new. It is in the table as the comparison ruler every other shape is read against: a table with the live shape missing cannot say what changed. Drawn by torsoPartsV2 at tier one, design one, so it is today's barrel and not a redrawing of it.

shapes.name: Toolbox
shapes.prompt: a squared toolbox body with a wide flat lid across the top that overhangs a much narrower case below it, a seam where the lid meets the case, corners softened but not round, no neck
shapes.notes: the only shape in the table that steps IN as it goes down, and the step is a real edge in the silhouette rather than a groove drawn on a barrel. Its case is the narrowest waist in the table, which is what makes the lid read as a lid and not as a shoulder.

shapes.name: Teapot
shapes.prompt: a rounded teapot body, narrow at the shoulders and swelling out to a low rounded belly, tucked in to a flat base, with one small spout stub low on its left side, no neck
shapes.notes: the only shape with no straight side anywhere: its widest row sits low, below the middle, where every other shape in the table is widest at the top or the same all the way down. The spout is a STUB, a short nub off the belly and never a handle loop, because an enclosed hole is see-through and the clay law forbids it.

shapes.name: Engine
shapes.prompt: a squared engine block body, a big flat-sided casting with square shoulders and softly bevelled corners, a raised cover panel across the chest and three ribs below it, the same width all the way down, no neck
shapes.notes: the biggest and squarest thing in the table, at the top of the width band and near the top of the height band, and the only one whose width never changes from shoulder to base. It carries the table's distance the cheap way, by area: every other shape sits inside it.

arm.formPhrase: a stubby vertical limb, straight up and down, three times as long as it is wide, a plain rounded cap at the top end and a simple rounded mitt hand at the bottom, perfectly symmetric left to right

shapes.name: Mitts
shapes.prompt: a stubby vertical limb, straight up and down, a plain rounded cap at the top end, a rounded elbow ball with a band across it, a wrist cuff, and a round mitt hand with a thumb at the bottom
shapes.notes: the live arm's family, redrawn. It is NOT the v2 ruler: that one measures armL 0.268 against a band that stops at 0.263, so carrying it would put an out-of-band shape in a table whose whole claim is that no rule moves for it. The fist is pulled up the shaft until the band is met, and nothing else about the family changes.

shapes.name: Claws
shapes.prompt: a plain vertical tube limb with a rounded cap at the top end, no elbow, a shallow collar at the wrist, and a two-finger gripper hand at the bottom whose thick fingers spread outward and then curl back in toward each other
shapes.notes: the fingers CLOSE. Two that only spread read as a trolley on the contact sheet; two that come back toward each other read as a claw. The arm itself is a plain tube, because the mitt's character is its stack of mouldings and the claw's is the absence of them. The palm is a round boss and the hand pivot sits inside it, so the fingers can open below that row without the pivot landing in air.

shapes.name: Pincers
shapes.prompt: a thin vertical stick limb, much slimmer than a normal arm, a small rounded cap at the top end, one narrow band at the elbow and one at the wrist, ending in two long straight thin prongs that open into a wide fork
shapes.notes: the thin one, and its point is how little ink it has: at ring size it reads as a stick with a fork on the end and never as a limb with a hand. The widest row on it is the OPEN FORK and not the shoulder cap, because a cap sized to the contract's armW on a shaft this thin is a lollipop, which is what the first cut drew.

shapes.name: Tube
shapes.prompt: a chunky concertina bellows limb, a stack of soft rings of two alternating widths so the edge is scalloped, no elbow, no wrist and no fingers, ending in a plain rounded stub
shapes.notes: no hand at all, which is the one thing no other arm in the table does. It is also the widest and the shortest, so the two arms with a hand blob at the bottom cannot be confused with it. The rings overlap so the part stays one blob with no enclosed hole.
